subject: whether it's a good idea to include flags and if-blocks in Stan code

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: whether it's a good idea to include flags and if-blocks in Stan code
parts:
Hi—somebody, Bob I think it was, told me it’s a bad idea to put blocks of code within if-statements, this sort of thing:

if (flag){
. . .
. . .
}

where “flag” is then passed in as data, and ypu pass in a 1 if you want that section of code to be run. Bob was saying this is a bad idea, it’s better just to have new Stan programs.

I just want to say that, from the user’s perspective, this can be tricky. In a lot of my work now I’ll have 5, say, very slightly different Stan programs—the basic model is the same but there are some differences for example with error distributions or priors or auxiliary data. It’s not so horrible to have 5 different programs. But then if I need to make a change, I have to go thru and edit all 5. This is a recipe for error and it violates the “never duplicate your code” principle. It’s possible that some of this could be ameliorated using functions. But for now, I have to say that if-blocks are a convenient way for me to keep some control over my sprawling workspace.

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] whether it's a good idea to include flags and if-blocks in Stan code
parts:
Yes, that was me. I agree that cut-and-paste is really bad
news. It's nearly impossible to maintain. And also hard to
understand. Making code readable is very important.

What I was objecting to in particular about Andrew's use of
conditional model blocks was that in one of the branches, there was a
parameter that wasn't used. Andrew's Stan program was something like

|
parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> theta;
...
model {
if (cond) {
theta ~ ...;
}
...
|

where the only use of the parameter theta in the model was inside
the conditional. Andrew could get away with this trick because theta
is constrained and thus has a proper posterior even with no sampling
statement in the model. But this trick won't work if theta is
unconstrained, because the posterior will be improper.

What we really need is a way to encapsulate the use and the declaration
together. Then we could have something like a grouped predictor,
associated parameter vector, and linear predictor term modularly
declared as data, parameter, and term in the model. But I have no idea
how to modularize that way.

- Bob
